thread.title: A Landlord's Dream - High Return With Lower Risk - Ventas Inc. (NYSE:VTR)

author: Jussi Askola
title: A Landlord's Dream - High Return With Lower Risk - Ventas Inc. (NYSE:VTR)
text:
Source
Investing capital is all about balancing risks and returns. In this sense, landlords are no different. They seek to achieve returns by buying properties generating rents and possibly appreciation in the long run. Sounds simple, but it really isn’t. While forecasting short-term returns/rents may be fairly straightforward, estimating the long-term risk of properties is very challenging. And just like any other business, some landlords are just better at it than others.
Ventas ( VTR ) has been the gold standard of landlords at achieving high returns relative to its business risk over the last 2 decades:
Ventas did not just beat the market returns by a very wide margin, but it did so while taking less than average business risk. Efficient market theorists teach us that higher returns can only be earned by taking excess risk, and yet Ventas did the exact opposite. But risk is subjective in its nature, so let me explain why I consider Ventas to be a lower risk company:
It owns a widely diversified portfolio of healthcare-oriented properties that are of the highest quality. Such properties earn highly consistent and predictable income with relatively low tenant turnover, overbuilding risk, or government-pay risk. The demand drivers of healthcare properties are very sustainable given the fast-aging demographics of the USA. Occasional oversupply is set to happen, but over the long run, the demand is expected to grow massively. Finally, the ultimate proof that this is a lower risk business is that not even the great financial crisis of 2008-2009 could stop the growth machine. While most businesses suffered large deteriorations in fundamentals, Ventas managed to fare well in the mid of the crisis. Put in other words, this is a recession-resistant business that suffers less from downcycles, and has strong long-term growth potential as the US population keeps aging and the demand for senior-housing and other healthcare-assets continues to rise.
Ventas has been aggressively capitalizing on this superior risk-to-reward business and grown to become the leading healthcare REIT along with HCP ( HCP ) and Welltower ( WELL ). The difference here is that Ventas has historically achieved much greater success than its peers thanks to a greater focus on quality, a cost of capital advantage, and arguably a superior management team:
As you can see in the above chart, the long-term growth has been phenomenal, but it has slowed down in the recent past. In 2017, the FFO per share growth was minimal and it is expected to remain on a low side this year again. This has gotten the investment community worried and resulted in a massive sell-off in the latest quarters:
As a result, the dividend yield is also at close to its 5-year high level:
I consider this to be an opportunity to invest in a lower-risk business trading at an unusually high dividend yield.
The growth has come down, there is no denying that. Ventas is facing some real challenges, that is also true. Nonetheless, there is a point where valuation becomes overly depressed and we have reached this point with Ventas selling at a close to 6% yield and just 13 times FFO.
I don’t expect the growth to ever return to the 10% annual average, but just 5% would go a very long way and I believe this to be a very realistic expectation. The reasons why the growth is currently stagnating is because the NOI growth rate of its assets, particularly the senior housing portfolio, is deteriorating due the increased supply of new properties in its market. Moreover, Ventas is currently undertaking a portfolio repositioning by disposing some of its higher-yielding (but riskier) – creating dilution over the short run.
What is important to understand here is that these challenges are temporary in nature, and not permanent ones. For one, oversupply won’t last forever with the fast-aging demographics; and for two, the dilution from dispositions ends when the capital is reallocated into new investments.
So rather than worrying about the short-term picture, I prefer to take a longer-term perspective and focus on what matters: Ventas owns the highest quality properties in a lower risk market that is expected to achieve significant growth over the next many decades. NOI will fluctuate in the short run, but the big picture looks very bright in terms of growth:
As the overbuilding dissipates itself, and the NOI growth accelerates, I expect Ventas to regain a more positive sentiment from the investment community. Sooner or later, I expect Ventas to surpass its latest 52-week highs of $72.36 per share which is 33% higher than today’s share price.
Final Thoughts Ventas is a growth-machine that suffers from temporary challenges. This is nothing unusual. In fact, even the very best franchises including Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO ), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ) or even Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ) do occasionally run into troubles - causing their share price to tumble amid short-term difficulties.
I believe that Ventas can easily sustain these temporary challenges, and this is why I am bullish. The close to 6% dividend yield is well covered at a 75% payout ratio and given that Ventas has never ever cut its dividend (not even during the 2000 or the 2008 debacles), I consider it to be very defensive.
I will in the next weeks be on the look-out for other defensive REIT investments. If you enjoyed this article and wish to receive updates on my latest research, click " Follow " next to my name at the top of this article.
